title: A lamp in a windless place

verses.sa: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः । मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥
verses.tr: The yogi, with a peaceful mind, free of fear, and firm in celibate discipline, restrains the mind, fixes awareness on Me, and sits devoted to Me as the supreme aim.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The previous verse fixed the body, and this one turns to the inner conditions of the mind before it can rest in peace.

body.text: The yogi, with a peaceful mind, free of fear, and firm in celibate discipline, restrains the mind, fixes awareness on Me, and sits devoted to Me as the supreme aim. The word madhuparah, for whom I am the supreme aim, shows that the yogi's meditation is directed toward Krishna as the highest goal, and this devotion is the very purpose of his sitting. Krishna now says that by keeping the mind united in this way, the yogi attains the supreme peace that comes from Him.

verses.sa: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः । शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥
verses.tr: The disciplined yogi, always uniting the mind in this way, attains the supreme peace of freedom rooted in Me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the physical discipline of yoga. Now he tells Arjuna what this steady practice actually produces.

body.text: The disciplined yogi, always uniting the mind in this way, attains the supreme peace of freedom rooted in Me. Listen to the word shanti, peace. Here it is the supreme freedom that ends all inner disturbance and rests in the divine. Krishna now turns to the daily habits that either build or break this steady mind.

verses.sa: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
verses.tr: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who eats nothing at all. It is not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who stays awake too long, Arjuna.
verses.angle: Yoga does not belong to the glutton or the starving
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that the practice of yoga cannot survive on an empty stomach or an overfed one. Listen to what he says next.

body.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who eats nothing at all. It is not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who stays awake too long, Arjuna. Krishna names four extremes, too much, too little, too much sleep, too much wakefulness, and says yoga is not for any of them. He then tells Arjuna that yoga that destroys suffering comes from a balanced life.

verses.sa: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
verses.tr: Yoga that destroys suffering comes from balanced eating, balanced activity, balanced work, and balanced sleep and waking.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna lists four things that must be balanced. Listen to the last one, the one about sleep and waking, and hear what it promises.

body.text: Yoga that destroys suffering comes from balanced eating, balanced activity, balanced work, and balanced sleep and waking. Measured food, measured effort, measured sleep and waking: from these, yoga that ends sorrow becomes possible. Krishna now moves from balanced living to the mind itself, describing what a controlled mind resting in the true self looks like.

verses.sa: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते । निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥
verses.tr: When the controlled mind rests in the true self alone and is free from craving for all pleasures, that person is called united in yoga.
verses.angle: Resting in the true self alone
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now tells Arjuna how to recognize true yoga. Listen for the mark of a mind that has found its home.

body.text: When the controlled mind rests in the true self alone and is free from craving for all pleasures, that person is called united in yoga. The controlled mind rests in the true self alone, and the person is called united in yoga. The mind does not rest on objects, but on the self alone. Krishna compares this steady mind to a lamp that does not flicker in a windless place.

verses.sa: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
verses.tr: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so the disciplined mind of a yogi does not waver while practicing yoga of the true self.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his teaching on the yogi's steady mind by giving it a single, clear image of a lamp.

body.text: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so the disciplined mind of a yogi does not waver while practicing yoga of the true self. A lamp in a windless place does not flicker, and that is the yogi's steadied mind. When that steadiness is fully reached, the person rests in the true self alone and is free from all craving.

verses.sa: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥
verses.tr: When the restrained mind becomes still through yoga practice, and the person sees the true self by the true self, one is content in the true self alone.
verses.angle: Yatra: the state where the mind rests
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: What does it feel like to be truly at peace? Listen to how the state of yoga is described.

body.text: When the restrained mind becomes still through yoga practice, and the person sees the true self by the true self, one is content in the true self alone. The verse repeats yatra, meaning where, to describe a single state. In that state, the restrained mind rests, and the true self sees the true self, and is content there. Krishna then explains that this boundless joy is beyond the senses and grasped by the mind.

verses.sa: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् । वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥
verses.tr: One knows the boundless joy beyond the senses and grasped by the discerning mind; established in it, one never truly falls away.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that the highest joy is beyond the senses, grasped only by the mind, and once reached, a person never truly falls away.

body.text: One knows the boundless joy beyond the senses and grasped by the discerning mind; established in it, one never truly falls away. The word atyantikam means boundless or ultimate. The verse says this joy is grasped by the mind and is beyond the senses, so the yogi who reaches it stands firm and never wavers from truth. Krishna says that once a person finds this state, they feel no greater gain exists, and they are not shaken by sorrow.

verses.sa: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥
verses.tr: Having attained it, one thinks no greater gain exists. Established in it, one is not shaken even by great sorrow.
verses.angle: labham, gain, and why it is supreme
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks you to notice one gain, and why no other gain can match it. Listen for how heavy sorrow is treated.

body.text: Having attained it, one thinks no greater gain exists. Established in it, one is not shaken even by great sorrow. The word is labham, gain. Krishna says that once you have this, you consider no other gain greater than that. It is a state where even heavy sorrow, duhkhena, cannot shake you. Krishna now names this state: know it as yoga, the severance of union with suffering.

verses.sa: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥
verses.tr: Know that as yoga: the severance of union with suffering. Practice that yoga with certainty, with an undiscouraged mind.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the peace that meditation brings, and now he gives it a name. Listen for how he defines yoga.

body.text: Know that as yoga: the severance of union with suffering. Practice that yoga with certainty, with an undiscouraged mind. Here, Krishna names yoga as the severance from union with suffering. The word yoga points to the ending of the mind's bond with sorrow, and he commands that it be practiced with certainty and without discouragement. He then urges that this practice be undertaken with certainty and a mind that has not lost heart.

verses.tr: Abandon every desire born of resolve, and restrain the whole field of the senses on all sides with the mind alone.
verses.angle: The mind alone gathers the scattered senses
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells us to drop the desires that spring from our own plans, and to pull the senses back with the mind alone.

body.text: Abandon every desire born of resolve, and restrain the whole field of the senses on all sides with the mind alone. The verse names one tool, manas, the mind. It is not the senses that pull the senses back, but the mind acting alone that gathers them on all sides. Krishna then explains that this mind is quieted only little by little through steady discernment.

verses.sa: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
verses.tr: Little by little, the mind should be quieted by steady discernment. Fix the mind in the true self and think of nothing else.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has asked how to steady the mind. This verse gives the exact method. Listen to the steps.

body.text: Little by little, the mind should be quieted by steady discernment. Fix the mind in the true self and think of nothing else. Krishna says to use buddhi, the discerning mind, and hold it with dhriteh, firmness. First you quiet the mind, then you place it in the true self, and only then you stop thinking at all. Krishna now says to bring the wandering mind back into the true self.

verses.sa: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
verses.tr: Whenever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, bring it back under the control of the true self.
verses.angle: Yato yato: the repeated wandering of the mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna knows the mind will keep slipping away. Listen to the exact instruction for bringing it back.

body.text: Whenever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, bring it back under the control of the true self. The Sanskrit repeats yato yato, wherever, which means the mind will wander again and again. The remedy is just as plain: bring it back to the true self, and only to the true self. The yogi who masters this wandering mind is the one who reaches the highest joy.

verses.sa: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥
verses.tr: The yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion is stilled, and who is free from impurity attains the highest joy.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is teaching Arjuna how to master the restless mind. Listen for the word that describes the mind once it is completely stilled.

body.text: The yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion is stilled, and who is free from impurity attains the highest joy. The word is shantarajasam, with passion stilled. Passion here is the restless force that pushes the mind to constantly seek and grasp, and when it settles, the yogi reaches the highest joy. Krishna then describes how the yogi who has become Brahman and is spotless reaches that joy.
